ⲥⲱⲧⲡ̄ + ⲧⲏⲛⲉ '(I have) chosen you'; cognate with following ⲧⲙⲛⲧⲥⲱⲧⲡ̄
ⲉⲕⲕⲗⲏⲥⲓⲁ ⲉⲧⲟⲩⲁⲃⲉ 'the holy church' standard formula
ⲭⲟ/ϫⲟ 'sow' regularly governs ⲡⲃⲣⲉ 'the seed' in this kephalaion
ⲭⲛ̄ = ϫⲛ̄/ϣⲁ ⲡⲉⲓⲉⲃⲧ 'from the East'; the directional pair ⲡⲉⲓⲉⲃⲧ–ⲡⲉⲙⲛⲧ 'East–West' is fixed
ⲧⲁⲍⲉⲗⲡⲓⲥ 'my hope' completes the prepositional phrase
ⲧⲏⲣⲟⲩ ⲛ̄ⲧⲟⲓⲕⲟⲩⲙⲉⲛⲏ 'all of the inhabited world' is the standard formula
ⲥⲁⲟⲩⲛⲉⲙ '(at the) right hand' standard pair with ⲡⲁⲧⲟⲩⲃⲟⲩⲣ 'left hand'
ⲡⲉⲓ̈ⲁⲏ 'because' regularly opens explanatory clause; ⲡ- article required for ⲡⲛⲁ
ⲛⲉϥⲙⲁⲑⲏⲧⲏⲥ 'his disciples'; the relative perfect ⲛ̄ⲧⲁⲣⲉ requires the disciples as subject
completes ⲛⲉϩⲙⲁⲑⲏⲧⲏⲥ 'his disciples' across line break

notes.decision: Translated 'farmer' (peasant/cultivator). Lycopolitan ⲁⲣⲙⲟⲩⲧⲉ corresponds to Sahidic ⲣⲙ̄ϩⲱⲧⲉ or similar — the agricultural laborer who tills, sows, and reaps. Used interchangeably here with ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲉ (line 5, 26).
Translated 'seed.' Lycopolitan ⲃⲣⲉ = Sahidic ϭⲣⲟϭ/ϣⲣⲏ 'seed.' The compound ⲛ̄ⲉⲛ̄ⲃⲣⲉ ⲛⲉⲏ[ⲧϥ] = 'seeds of his own' or possibly 'new seeds' depending on what fills the lacuna.
Translated 'select' (sift, examine, pick out). Lycopolitan ⲭⲱⲗⲙⲉ = Sahidic ϫⲱⲗⲙ 'examine, sift through,' with the sense of careful agricultural selection of seed.
Translated 'harvest/summer.' ϣⲱⲙ = 'summer' = harvest time. Antithetical to ⲡⲣⲱ 'winter' in line 19. The seasonal pair structures the metaphor.
Translated 'season.' Lycopolitan form for 'season, fitting time' — distinct from but parallel to Greek ⲕⲁⲓⲣⲟⲥ used in same line.
Translated 'reap.' ⲱⲉⲥ = ⲱϩⲥ 'reap, harvest.' Recurs in line 28.

Translated 'casts them into the granary.' ⲡϣⲏⲛ here is the storage place / barn (literally 'tree' but used metaphorically for storehouse, or possibly read as ⲡⲉⲥⲣⲱ 'storehouse'). Tentative — the standard parable image of gathering grain into the barn fits.
Translated 'likening themselves.' Reflexive use of ⲧⲛ̄ⲧⲱⲛ 'compare, liken.' The apostles liken themselves to the form of the world they enter.
Translated 'lordship.' ⲙⲛⲧ-ⲛⲁⲃ (abstract from ⲛⲁⲃ 'lord'/'master') = 'lordship.' Recurs in line 12.
Both translated 'beforehand/in advance.' Lycopolitan ⲥⲁ-ⲉⲏⲧ = 'in front, beforehand'; ⲉⲁⲧⲉⲉⲏ = ⲉⲧⲉⲏ 'before, in advance.' The repetition emphasizes prior preparation.
Translated 'winter.' ⲡⲣⲱ from older ⲡⲉ-ⲣⲟⲙⲡⲉ-related forms; the contrast with ⲡϣⲱⲙ 'summer' in line 20 confirms the seasonal pair. ⲁⲥⲉϥ̄ here likely = 'damages it' — winter damages the fruit.
Translated 'head/sheaf.' Lycopolitan ⲁⲁⲡⲉ = ⲁⲡⲉ 'head' — here in agricultural register: the head of grain / the sheaf. Recurs line 29.
Translated 'walking downward.' ⲙⲁⲉⲉ (Lyc.) = ⲙⲟⲟϣⲉ 'walk'; ⲁⲡⲓⲧⲛⲉ = 'downward, below.' Spatial-soteriological: the apostle descends to the world.
Translated 'his new church.' ⲣⲙⲉⲉ here = 'new' (Lycopolitan reflex of ⲃⲣ̄ⲣⲉ 'new'). The 'new church' is the community formed by the latest apostle in the succession.
Mid-line scribal vacat marks structural break before 'Thus is the farmer' resumption. Split into two segments with break_after on first.
Translated 'measure.' ⲟⲩⲓ̈ⲧⲉ = ⲟⲉⲓⲧ 'measure, allotment.' The farmer apportions nourishment to the planting/harvest.
Translated 'reaches.' ⲡⲱⲉ = ⲡⲱϩ 'reach, attain, arrive.' Used here of time reaching the farmer (ⲉⲡⲱⲉ ⲁⲡⲁⲣⲙⲟⲩⲧⲉ 'reaches to the farmer').

Translated 'the molding of humanity.' Greek loanword πλάσμα = 'thing molded, formed creature' — technical Manichaean term for the formation of Adam/humanity by the archons. ⲙⲛⲧⲣⲱⲙⲉ = 'humanity/manhood.'
Translated 'the upper place first/of the first.' ⲡⲥⲁⲛⲧⲡⲉ = 'the upper region/heaven.' ⲛϣⲁⲣⲡ̅ = 'first/foremost,' here qualifying either the upper place or the time-frame.

Translated 'depart upward' (consistently paired with ⲁⲍⲣⲏⲓ̈ 'upward' throughout: lines 2, 5, 14, 20-21). Likely Lycopolitan reflex of a verb meaning 'to be raised, to ascend'; possibly related to ϫⲓⲥⲉ 'raise' (cf. accumulated ⲡⲭⲥⲉ 'the Height') with ⲧϩ̄ ending. The semantic context — apostolic ascent out of the world — confirms an upward-motion verb. Rendered as 'depart upward' to capture both motion and direction.

Translated 'to lordship'. ⲛⲁⲃ = Lycopolitan/Old-Coptic form of ⲛⲏⲃ 'lord, master' (cf. line 6 ⲙ̄ⲛ̄ⲭⲱⲥ 'without master'); ⲙⲛⲧ- abstract prefix yields 'lordship/dominion'. The apostle 'goes to lordship in the world for this time' — i.e., he assumes oversight of his church.

Translated 'without master, without shepherd'. ⲭⲱⲥ likely contracted ⲭⲁⲩⲥ/ϫⲟⲉⲓⲥ 'lord/master'; ϣⲉ = ϣⲱⲥ 'shepherd'. The double phrase parallels the institutional concern: the church must never be left without leadership of either pastoral or magisterial kind.
Translated 'glad of heart' (= Sahidic ⲟⲩⲣⲟⲧ ⲛ̄ϩⲏⲧ 'rejoice in heart'). The farmer's joy at harvest is the typological link to the apostle's joy at his church's fruitfulness.

Translated 'the multiplication of his vessels of import'. ⲕⲱⲃ 'doubling, increase'; ⲡⲉϩⲛⲁⲃ likely Lyc. for ⲡⲉϥ-ϩⲛⲁⲩ 'his vessels' (ⲍⲛⲁⲁⲩ 'containers, wares'); ⲛⲉⲟⲩⲉⲓⲛ = ⲛ̄-ⲉⲓⲛⲉ 'of bringing/import'. The merchant's profit metaphor.

Translated 'the month of Phaōphi'. ⲡⲁⲁⲡⲉ here is the Coptic month name Phaōphi/Paope (October-November), the autumn storage month, paired with Pharmouthi (April) in line 32-33. Note: ⲡⲁⲁⲡⲉ also = 'head/sheaf' in this kephalaion's vocabulary; a double-reading 'month of the sheaf' would also fit semantically.

Lycopolitan ϩⲓⲣⲁⲧϥ̄ 'at his foot, at his side, beside.' In the context of one apostle being sent ⲍⲓⲣⲉⲧϩ ⲛⲧⲕⲉⲉⲕⲕⲗⲏⲥⲓⲁ — 'at the foot of / over' the next Church — the idiom denotes assignment or oversight. Rendered 'to oversee' to capture the supervisory sense.
Read as ϣⲁϥϩⲱⲡ̄ 'they conceal / are concealed' (habitual + ϩⲱⲡ 'hide'). The ⲙⲟⲣⲫⲁⲩⲉ ('forms', plural of μορφή) of the Church-of-Free-Ones are kept hidden in the Height before each apostle's descent.

Lycopolitan ϩⲱⲱϥ ⲁⲛ = 'himself also / himself again.' The apostle 'himself comes down again' to manifest. Could alternately read ⲍⲱϩ as standalone particle 'also'; chose 'himself again' as more idiomatic to context of recurring descent.
ⲛ-ⲧⲟⲩⲱ — purposive infinitive 'to raise.' Mandated rendering 'raise' preserves the upward soteriological direction. Paired with ⲛⲁϩⲙⲉⲥ ('to save them from the flesh').
ⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁϭ 'greatness, majesty.' Standard Manichaean title 'Son of the Greatness' for Jesus = υἱὸς τοῦ Μεγέθους.

Greek πνευματικόν 'spiritual.' The phrase 'in a spiritual (way), in a body' captures the Manichaean Christology of Christ's docetic-yet-corporeal mode of incarnation, immediately glossed by ⲭⲱⲣⲓⲥ ⲥⲱⲙⲁ 'without a body' in line 24.

ⲛⲟ̄ⲁⲟⲩⲁⲛ analyzed as ⲛ̄-ⲟⲩⲁ-ⲟⲩⲁⲛ 'of one of someone' or simply 'of a person/somebody.' This phrase echoes Phil 2:7 (μορφὴν δούλου / σχῆμα ὡς ἄνθρωπος); but the Coptic here does not use the Lycopolitan word for slave (ⲍⲙϩⲁⲗ) but rather a generic indefinite. Translated 'a form of someone' to preserve the indefiniteness while ⲥⲭⲏⲙⲁ ⲛⲑⲉ ⲛ̄ⲛⲓⲣⲱⲙⲉ ('appearance like that of men') glosses it.

Likely Coptic reflex of Greek δῆμος 'people, populace, community,' with epenthetic -ⲣ- (or possibly conflation with δρόμος 'circuit, jurisdiction'). The three occurrences (lines 27, 30, 32) are consistent with 'the people of the Jews' as a collective community: Christ revealed himself in it, Satan entered into it, Judas accused before it. Rendering 'the people' rather than 'doctrine' (δόγμα).

ⲁϩⲡ̄ from ϣⲱⲡ 'receive'; ⲡⲱⲕ ⲛϩⲏⲧ — Lycopolitan idiom for 'turn/inclination of heart' = 'purpose, will, intent.' 'He received the heart's purpose of his Father (who sent him into the world)' = he took up the Father's commission.
ⲛⲟⲩϫⲉ 'cast, throw.' The Evil One 'cast envy' into the people of the Jews — a transitive action of injection. Standard Manichaean diabology of envy as cast pollutant.

Translated 'out from the dead.' The form ⲟⲩ here is an unusual reading; expected would be ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ϩⲛ̄ ⲛⲉⲧⲙⲁⲩⲧ or ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ⲛ̄ϩⲏⲧ⸗. Could be Lycopolitan variant or scribal. The sense 'from among the dead' is unambiguous.
'He breathed into their face.' ⲁϩⲣⲉⲩ = 'into their face/upon them'; the directional particles preserve the literal Johannine ἐνεφύσησεν action (John 20:22).

'He raised himself up.' ⲝⲉⲥⲧ⸗ = Sahidic ϫⲉⲥⲧ⸗ (causative of ϫⲓⲥⲉ 'be high'). The reflexive raising preserves the active-emission/ascent quality central to Manichaean cosmology — Jesus does not 'ascend' passively but enacts his own raising.

Rendered 'they were all put to shame.' The verbal compound ⲣ̄- + ⲙⲛ̄ⲧⲁϣⲓⲡⲉ literally 'do shame-state.' Context (subject = apostles, who then ascend to the Greatness) suggests their experience of disgrace/persecution in the world before being raised; could alternatively mean 'they all suffered modesty/humility' but 'were put to shame' is the most defensible reading from the morphology.
Greek loanword σκανδαλίζω 'cause to stumble, take offense.' Translated 'stumbled' to preserve the moral-fall image rather than 'were scandalized.'

'The path that is alive, that is narrow.' ⲗⲁⲝⲉ = Lycopolitan reflex of ⲗⲱϫϫ 'narrow, oppressed,' contrasting with ⲟⲩⲉⲥⲧⲁⲛⲧ 'wide' (line 29). Echoes Matthew 7:13-14 directly. The 'living path' = the way of righteousness.

Rendered 'they ruined the Church.' ⲣ̄ⲧⲁⲕ = abbreviated ⲣ̄ⲧⲁⲕⲟ 'cause to perish, ruin, destroy.' Subject is unspecified persecutors/heretics; the contrast with 'but they themselves [the righteous men of truth] were raised up' in line 33 confirms this negative reading.

'Ceased, failed.' Lycopolitan reflex of ⲱϫⲛ 'cease, fail, come to an end.' Subject is 'the Church' continued from previous line. The historiographical pattern: Church declines after righteous men depart, then world draws back without restraint.

'Drew back.' ⲥⲱⲝⲧ̄ = Lycopolitan reflex of ⲥⲱϣⲧ̄ 'turn aside, draw back'; ⲁⲡⲁϩⲟⲩ = 'backward, behind.' Together: 'drew backward' — i.e., the world reverted/regressed without the constraining presence of the righteous.
ⲕⲱⲧϩ here = Sahidic ⲕⲱⲧϥ 'pluck, gather' (of fruit). The pairing with ⲃⲓ 'carry off' and the object ⲕⲁⲣⲡⲟⲥ 'fruits' confirms agricultural sense: the tree is stripped. Not 'surround' (ⲕⲱⲧⲉ).
ⲡⲭⲓⲥⲉ (Lycopolitan) = ⲡϫⲓⲥⲉ 'the Height'. Per accumulated vocabulary: the upper cosmological pole. Refers here to Christ's ascension after the resurrection.
Relative perfect 2pl from ϣⲓⲛⲉ 'ask, inquire' + ⲉⲧⲃⲏⲧⲥ̄ 'about it' (referring back to apostleship). 'That which you have asked about' — Mani is answering his disciples' question.

Abbreviation of παράκλητος 'Paraclete' (with overstroke). Translated 'Paraclete' to preserve the Johannine technical term central to Manichaean self-understanding (Mani as the Paraclete promised by Jesus).
Lycopolitan ϩⲓⲣⲉⲧ⸗ + 2pl suffix = 'unto your feet / into your presence'. Translated 'unto you' for English idiom while preserving the directional sense.

Lycopolitan future III prefix ϩⲁ- + ϫⲡⲓⲟ 'convict, reprove'. The whole sequence is a paraphrase of John 16:8 ('the Paraclete will convict the world concerning sin, righteousness and judgment'), confirming the restoration [ⲡⲛⲁⲃⲉ] in line 9.
ⲍⲧⲉ likely = ϩⲉ 'fall' (Lycopolitan with -ⲧⲉ ending obscure; possibly ϩⲱⲧⲉ 'fall'). Reading 'sinners who shall fall (under judgment)' fits the Johannine context. Tentative.
ⲃⲱⲗⲡ = 'reveal, uncover'; ⲁⲃⲁⲗ (= Sah. ⲉⲃⲟⲗ) is the directional particle. Together: 'reveal' (literally 'unveil outward'). Standard Manichaean revelatory vocabulary.

Difficult sequence. Probable parsing: ⲙ̄-ⲡⲉⲧ-ⲁϩⲥ(?)-ⲛ-ⲟⲩⲱⲛϩ — a relative form expressing 'that which had not been revealed' (matching the standard Manichaean self-description: Mani reveals what previous apostles left unrevealed). The form is grammatically opaque to me; rendered ad sensum.

Greek loanword προθεσμία 'appointed term, fixed time-limit' (with Coptic phonetic/orthographic shift θ→ⲫ). Translated 'appointed term' to capture the legal-eschatological sense (the appointed span of all the years from Jesus to Mani).
ⲉⲓⲣⲉ 'do, make' + 3pl + ⲛ̄-ⲣⲙ̄ϩⲉ 'as free-persons'. Idiom 'make them free' = manumit / set free. Lycopolitan ⲍⲉ = ϩⲉ.
ⲁ- (purpose) + ⲥⲱⲧⲉ 'redeem, ransom' + ⲛ-ⲙ̄ⲧⲩⲭⲁⲩⲉ (definite plural 'the souls'; ⲙ̄- = Lycopolitan plural article variant). 'For the redemption of the souls' — soteriological technical phrase.

ϣⲃⲱⲛ — meaning here uncertain. The agricultural/seasonal context (Pharmouthi = April, harvest month in Egypt) suggests 'ripening' or 'change/turn (of season)'. Tentatively rendered 'the ripening reaches its fullness'. Crum lists ϣⲃⲱⲛ only as 'sickness, scab', which would not fit. Possibly a specialised harvest term, or scribal variant.
Causative-purpose: ⲁ- + ⲧ- (causative) + ⲟⲩⲁⲍ⸗ 'set, place' + 3pl. 'To set/establish them'. In context this is the gathering/setting of the souls in the appointed redemptive moment.

ⲧⲁ- = 1sg possessive feminine + Greek εἰκών 'image' = 'my image' (the bodily image Mani wears). ⲉⲧⲣ̄ⲫⲟⲣⲉⲓ ⲙ̄ⲙⲁⲥ = 'in which I wear it' (relative + causative + Greek φορεῖν 'wear, bear'). The image = Mani's own incarnate form, parallel to the Church wearing the flesh in line 24.
Artabanus, king of Parthia — Artabanus IV/V, last Arsacid king. The historical frame is Mani's birth and youth under late Parthian rule, transitioning to the Sasanian period under Ardashir.

Three 1sg perfects: 'I was nourished' (ⲥⲁⲛⲉϣ qual. of ⲥⲁⲛⲱϣ 'nurture'), 'I grew up' (ⲁⲓⲁⲓ 'increase'), 'I reached/arrived at' (ⲡⲱϩ). Mani's autobiographical voice: nourished, grown, arrived at the season's fulfillment.
'The perfection/completion of the season' — Mani reaches maturity precisely at the appointed time. ⲭⲱⲕ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ per accumulated vocabulary = 'perfection/completion'.

'The Living Paraclete came down (to me)'. ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲍ̄ = ⲉⲧⲁⲛϩ̄ 'the living'. This is the climactic moment of Mani's call — the descent of the Living Paraclete (Mani's heavenly Twin / Syzygos) at age 24 in the year of Ardashir's coronation. Foundational autobiographical datum.

ⲟⲩⲱⲗⲡ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ = 'reveal forth, uncover.' With ⲍⲁ ('concerning, regarding'), the construction is 'he revealed to me concerning X.' This anaphoric formula opens each item in Mani's catalogue of mysteries shown by the Paraclete.
Translated as 'the Deep' and 'the Height' — the cosmic vertical axis (νοῦν / ⲡⲭⲥⲉ = ⲡϫⲓⲥⲉ). These are paired cosmological extremes flanking Light/Darkness in the Manichaean catalogue.

ⲡⲟⲩⲧⲱⲧ from ⲧⲱⲧ ('agree, join') = 'their joining/agreement.' ⲥⲉⲍⲟ likely from ⲥⲱϩⲉ ('to draw, drag') — 'they were drawn up.' The image is of mixed elements being drawn upward into this cosmos through the joining of Light and Darkness.
Standard idiom 'open my eyes' = reveal/enlighten (per accumulated vocabulary). Preserves the literal eye-rousing image even where 'reveal' would smooth.
ⲭⲏⲩ = ϫⲏⲩ 'ships' — the cosmic vessels (sun and moon) that bear refined light upward. Standard Manichaean cosmological term.

ⲥⲱⲧϥ = 'refine, filter' (cf. ⲥⲁⲧϩ in accumulated vocabulary). The ships function to filter/refine the Light out of the mixture — this is the central cosmic function of the luminaries in Manichaean physics.
ⲍⲱⲱϥ ('itself') intensifies — 'the Erring itself,' i.e. the cosmic principle of Error in person, not merely an act of erring.
Greek loanword πλάσσειν 'to mold/form (clay).' Used here of Adam's creation; preserved as 'molding' to keep the demiurgic clay-imagery distinct from ⲙⲟⲩⲟⲩⲛⲕ and ⲙⲟⲣⲫⲏ.

Double brackets in transcription mark scribal dittography: the scribe began writing this clause, recognized it as a duplicate of lines 18–19, and cancelled it. Treated here as a restoration entry noting the cancellation; the running translation continues directly from ⲛⲟⲩⲉⲛⲧⲟⲗⲁⲩⲉ to the catechumens-mystery on line 17.
ⲧⲕⲟⲗⲁⲥⲓⲥ = Greek κόλασις 'punishment/chastisement.' ⲁⲏⲟ̄ ⲛⲉⲩ = 'set/laid upon them' (qualitative of ⲁϩⲉ 'to stand, set'). Renders the punishment as imposed.
Cognate-figura etymologica: 'reflection reflects upon it.' Preserves the verbal-noun pairing in English. ⲡⲙⲁⲕⲙⲉⲕ is the fifth faculty (per mandatory terminology).
'I beheld the All through him.' ⲡⲧⲏⲣϥ ('the All') is the Manichaean designation for the totality of cosmic reality; the Paraclete is the medium through whom Mani sees it whole.
'In the last years of Ardashir.' Marks the historical anchor: Mani's first public mission in the closing years of Ardashir I (d. 242 CE).
ⲭⲓⲟⲣⲉ = ϫⲓⲟⲟⲣ 'cross over (water), traverse.' Used twice on this page (here for the voyage to India, again on line 29 for the return). 'Crossed over' preserves the maritime sense.

ⲇⲉⲭⲉ = Greek δέχομαι 'receive, welcome.' ⲁϩⲍⲗⲗⲟ uncertain — possibly an auxiliary or a verbal idiom (perhaps 'he came to receive me') but the core meaning 'received me with great honor' is secure from ⲇⲉⲭⲉ ⲙⲙⲁⲓ̈ ⲍⲛ̄ ⲟⲩⲛⲁⲟ̄ ⲛⲧⲁⲓ̈ⲟ.

⳨ resolved as ⲣ̄: ⲁϥⲣ̄ ⲙⲁ ⲛⲏⲓ̈ = 'he made room/place for me' = idiom 'he gave me leave.' ⲧⲁⲙⲁⲍⲉ = ⲧⲁⲙⲁϩⲉ 'walking/traveling' (from ⲙⲟⲟϣⲉ). Idiom for granting freedom of travel within Shapur's domains.
Latin comitatus 'imperial retinue/court' transliterated through Greek κομιτᾶτον. Refers to Shapur's mobile royal court; Mani is described as accompanying it for many years.
